Challenge C088-CH2: Membranes in dairy plants foul quickly and need cleaning every week.
Detail: At two dairy plants we service — one near Temerin, one outside

content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Membrane fouling in dairy wastewater involves formation of compressible gel layers dominated by emulsified fats, which can be characterized through scanning electron microscopy, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and hydraulic resistance analysis.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08238","field":"abstract","quote":"Fouling layer composition was characterized by scanning electron microscopy, ATR-FTIR spectroscopy, and hydraulic resistance analysis"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-08240","field":"abstract","quote":"emulsified oil droplets constitute the primary foulant, forming a compressible gel layer"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Pre-treatment through feed screening at 200 micrometers can reduce total fouling resistance by 34% in fat-rich wastewater.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-08240","field":"abstract","quote":"Pre-screening of the feed stream through a 200 µm mesh reduced total fouling resistance by 34%"}]}]}
